name: GridMotion-TS-TW
title: Grid Motion
description: Four rows of photo and text tiles sit in a grid turned about fifteen degrees off level. Moving the pointer left or right shoves alternating rows in opposite directions with a soft lag.
use: A landing or portfolio section needs a wall of imagery that comes alive with the pointer.
avoid: You need tiles that stay still or legible on touch: rows only respond to a mouse and are always cropped at the edges.
a11y: Photos are CSS backgrounds with no alt text, and there is no reduced-motion path for the row drift. (keyboard: n-a, labels: none, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A dark backdrop holds a large four-by-seven grid of rounded square tiles, tilted counter-clockwise so its rows run diagonally. Most tiles are cropped photographs in muted tones; every fourth one is a black tile with a single white word.
behaves: Rows glide horizontally in alternating directions, drifting further the further the pointer sits from the middle, each row lagging a little differently. The grid is oversized, so its edges always run past the frame.
customise: Pass up to 28 items as strings, image URLs or nodes, plus the radial gradient colour. Row count, tilt, gap and slide range are fixed in the source.
weight: moderate: Twenty-eight tiles move with GSAP each tick, with no canvas or 3D scene.
demo: Camera bodies, forest windows, laptops, snowy peaks and black word tiles reading Depth, Flow and similar labels.
polishWhy: Well paced drift and a coherent tilt; outer tiles are always half cut off.
